subject.title: Cron agent runs can surface native Codex web_search missing-tool-result as a timeout-shaped cron failure

question: Should this issue wait for proof and resolution of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92847, or should maintainers queue a separate cron-surface repair for preserving embedded error causes after timeout cleanup?
rationale: Current main has partial fixes, but the remaining evidence spans an unmerged terminal-result timing PR and the cron timeout race; choosing the next canonical path depends on maintainer confidence in the proof gap.

options.title: Finish terminal-drain proof first
options.body: Require redacted real stream proof for the open terminal-drain PR, land or replace it if proven, then re-check whether the cron-visible timeout symptom remains.

options.title: Queue a separate cron handoff repair
options.body: Treat the cron wrapper as independently actionable and add a focused fix that preserves embedded run errors even when timeout cleanup wins the race.

options.title: Accept current partial fixes
options.body: Maintainers can decide the merged active-tool and attribution fixes are enough and close only after documenting why the delayed-result path is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Finish terminal-drain proof first
recommendation.body: Require redacted real stream proof for the open terminal-drain PR, land or replace it if proven, then re-check whether the cron-visible timeout symptom remains.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent main history and the open terminal-drain review both point to steipete as the strongest owner for the Codex app-server timing decision.
